findings.issue: In swap the VM's run loop is a separate internal function (entered with the continuation 4999 as a parameter) that the decompiler gives up on, so every instruction's effect (balances, invalidators, fees, TWAP state, Aqua pulls) is missing from swap; quote's copy of the same loop (internal_0x1356) is decompiled, with the opcode table resolved into an if-chain and the instructions inlined.
findings.rule: A jump to a value that is a parameter of an internal function, where every call site passes a constant (here 4999), is a return to that constant: specialise the function per call site (or treat the parameter as the return continuation) instead of aborting.

notes: Getters, invalidators, Ownable, rescueFunds, simulate, hash and eip712Domain were read line by line; quote, swap (3,630 lines) and the run-loop function internal_0x1356 (2,090 lines, recursive because instructions call ctx.runLoop() again, as in the source) were reviewed by structure. The 5 source loops are readable whiles in internal_0x1356: VM.runLoop (the opcode table lookup is resolved into an if-chain on the table's constants), Balances._staticBalancesXD, _loadBalances (as 'while True' with the bound test and an early exit), _initBalances, and Power.pow (3 inlined copies). swap's own copy of runLoop is lost (coverage finding). Copies are shown as copy lines (279), no copy loop. P10: many phis with SSA copies in one arm (instruction results); P8: keccak scratch stores beside symbolic mapping accesses.
summary: quote's VM run loop and its inlined instructions are decompiled faithfully with readable loops, but swap's run loop is aborted (all instruction effects lost there), twapLastSwaps members are misnamed as fixed arrays stor1/stor3, and 69 calls lose their function names to the mem[mem[64]] aliasing problem.
